description:
FILED s507b (Opus, 2026-10-04): the residue of #2686 (fixed in s507b: a run-time `require "./f.pl"` no longer runs
at compile time, and the fasl build no longer muffles STDOUT, so a `use`d module's printed output appears on run 1).

PROBES (worktree agent-abf54c6d69793c324, scratch/s507b/m3/, driver run2.pl = perl once, a FRESH script under pcl twice):
  pd.pl: `use lib "."; use WarnMod;` with WarnMod.pm = `warn "wm warn\n"; print STDERR "wm stderr\n"; ...`
     perl: wm warn / wm stderr / main v;  pcl run 1: wm stderr / main v  (the warn is LOST);  run 2 = perl.
  pc.pl: `BEGIN { print "b1\n" } use lib "."; use LocMod;` with LocMod.pm printing "LocMod body"
     perl: b1 / LocMod body / main v;  pcl run 1: LocMod body / b1 / main v;  run 2 = perl.
     (On main 08de9e4f run 1 AND run 2 lost "LocMod body" entirely.)
CAUSE (read): %p-build-module-fasl binds *error-output* to a broadcast stream (to hide compiler notes and the
"Undefined functions" summary) and p-warn writes to *error-output*; and under *pcl-fasl-build* a BEGIN block is
(:load-toplevel :execute) -- it fires at the fasl load -- while a `use` (p-eval-always) fires at COMPILE, so their
relative order inverts on the building run only.
FIX DIRECTIONS (not designed): (a) p-warn / the program's STDERR handle write to a stream captured at startup rather
than the dynamic *error-output*, so the build's muffle hides only the compiler; (b) for the ORDER: run the first run
from TEXT and build the fasl afterwards (needs an exit-time build hook: perl `exit` must not skip it), or keep
compile-time `use`s from executing module bodies (only their package creation is needed by the reader).


=== ADDED s507b (Opus 5.5, 2026-10-04) ===
Un-muffling the build's *standard-output* was TRIED and reverted: an import runs at the build's compile AND again
at the fasl load, so `use Test::More tests => 1` printed its plan twice (Pl/t/pcl-dash-m-01.t rows 4-5).  A fix
here has to make the import single (or the compile-time `use` body-free), not just un-muffle.

=== s508 (Fable, 2026-10-05): two more rows for this task's run-1 == run-2 == perl table, from the s507c PART ONE review probes ===
Probes mod-use, mod-use-first, mod-nested, mod-two, mod-twice, mod-eval-in in ~/pcl-agent-scratch/s508/review/ph.pl (IMPL TAG [REGEX]; answers in out/ph.perl / ph.base / ph.tree; perl 5.40.3, main fee16466, the s507c tree 0229e0ec) (each case is run twice in a fresh directory; the output file prints run 2 where it differs):
 1. On the cache-BUILDING run a `use`d module's load-time STDOUT is LOST entirely (its BEGIN block's print, its UNITCHECK's, its body's): run 1 of mod-use prints main:b first, run 2 and perl print M:begin / M:unitcheck / M:body before it.  (#2686, fixed by s507b, was the literal-`require "./f.pl"` half of this; a `use` still loses it.)
 2. On the cache-BUILDING run the ORDER of CHECK and INIT blocks across units is wrong although s507c's #2690 makes it right from run 2 on: mod-use run 1 = main:c2 / main:c1 / M:check (perl and run 2: main:c2 / M:check / main:c1); mod-two run 1 runs Q:init and M:init BEFORE main:i1.  The module's blocks reach the program's queue during the build pass and the program's own blocks are pushed on top of them at the load -- the same two-passes shape as this task's BEGIN-vs-`use` output order.


=== s509 (s507c resume, Opus) -- the forked first-run build is NOT shipped; this task stays OPEN ===
(a) What the fork did (s508, scratch/s507c/p2d/fr.pl: each case in a fresh dir with a fresh PCL_CACHE_DIR, run twice, STDOUT + STDERR + status vs perl 5.40.3; cases print-mod, warn-mod, begin-before-use, die-mod, bang-die, bang-die-use, end-exit, end-exit2, mod-use, mod-nested, mod-two, mod-twice, mod-eval-in).  Without the fork (the s507c tree): run 1 = perl in 4 of 13, run 2 in 11 of 13 -- print-mod, warn-mod, begin-before-use, mod-use, mod-nested, mod-two, mod-twice differ on run 1 only (a used module's load-time STDOUT/STDERR lost, a printing use ahead of an earlier BEGIN, CHECK/INIT order across units wrong).  With %p-build-script-fasl-apart (the script fasl compiled in a forked child, stdio /dev/null, exit :abort, reaped before user code; this image then LOADS the fasl as a later run does): run 1 == run 2 in all 13, 11 of 13 = perl (die-mod = #2740/#2764, mod-eval-in = #2762).
(b) Why it is not shipped (Fable s509, measured perl -> main -> the fork tree; probes copied to scratch/s507c/p2d/ruling/fr and fr2): the child runs every used module's BODY, so external side effects happen twice on run 1.
  - fr2/pid.pl (`use Pid;`, Pid.pm dies "already running" when run.pid exists, else writes it and unlinks it in an END block): perl and main print `working` on run 1 and run 2; the fork tree DIES on run 1 with `already running (pidfile run.pid exists)` plus a stray "While evaluating the form" line -- the child wrote the pidfile and left by :abort without its END block.
  - fr2/ask.pl (`use Ask;`, Ask.pm prompts on STDERR and re-reads STDIN until it gets a line): in the child STDIN is /dev/null, so an uncapped retry loop never ends (the capped copy: 6.3 s -> 10.4 s).
  - fr/s.pl (side-effect log): run 1 executes the module's body twice.  (Main's run 1 already runs `import` twice and the body before an earlier BEGIN block; that stays as it is.)
  A program that works on main and fails on its first run is not a trade for a first-run ordering fix.
(c) RULING: an EXACTLY-ONCE first run is the only acceptable fix; a design is owed by the reviewing session.  Two candidate directions, recorded as NOT yet designed: (1) run the building run from TEXT and build the cache afterwards in the image that already loaded the modules; (2) keep the in-process build and make the import single -- known counter-example: `sub first {...}` BEFORE `use List::Util 'first'`, where the load pass redefines the sub after a skipped import.  Nothing of the s508 #2702 work is kept (no part of it was exactly-once by construction on its own); its guard rows (script-cache-01.t rows 64-67 in the s508 extraction) were removed with it.
subject: A script's FIRST (cache-building) run: a `use`d module's `warn` at load time is LOST (the fasl build muffles *error-output*), and a printing `use` runs BEFORE an earlier BEGIN block's output (BEGIN is deferred to the fasl load); every later run matches perl
